trust_decision.summary: An unauthenticated request's Cookie header decides both the declared multipart part count N and the part index i, and therefore how much memory pkg/cookie/cookie.go allocates: numParts is parsed from the attacker-chosen cookie name and passed to make([]string, numParts), with the index used as cookieParts[i-1].

landing_point.why: The summary says 'Unbounded Multipart Cookie Allocation DoS'; the only size-driven allocation in the tree reachable from request data is make([]string, numParts) at cookie.go:130, with numParts taken verbatim from the cookie name at :126.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: No second site exists to dismiss; the only dismissal available is on the sink itself - README.md:277 says 'The VP cookie may be split into several cookies ... if you need it, you need it', which a solver could read as making an attacker-declared large part count legitimate and therefore uncappable.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Parts may arrive in any order: numParts is fixed by the first matching part seen, and indices then fill the slice, so a legitimate browser ordering that starts at 2ofN works. The write side also legitimately emits N parts for a large token (splitCookie, ~4000 bytes per part). A fix that requires 1ofN first, demands contiguous 1..N, or caps N below what splitCookie emits breaks legitimate split cookies.

O6_input_shapes: single cookie named exactly vouch.cookie.name (early return, unchanged)
multipart name <name>_<i>of<N> with N inside the accepted range
declared part count N greater than maxCookieParts (32)
declared part count N below 1 (0 or negative)
part index i greater than the declared N

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A part-aware ClearCookie that parses <i>of<N> to delete exactly the parts it set
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: it is the third function in the same file that already matches multipart cookie names by prefix and it copies the client-supplied name straight into a Set-Cookie header

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Applying the same split/rejoin treatment to the X-Vouch-Token / Authorization / querystring token sources
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: those sources hit the same header-size ceilings the cookie splitting exists for, so a maintainer mirroring the mechanism there is plausible

O9_family: unbounded memory allocation from an attacker-controlled size (CWE-789)

O10_build.project_tests: pkg/cookie/cookie_test.go:27 (TestSplitCookie) and :48 (TestCookie) cover this area directly; handlers/validate_test.go drives /validate through JWTCacheHandler -> FindJWT -> cookie.Cookie with httptest, no network

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Cap the declared part count only (`if numParts > 32 { return err }`) and miss that cookieParts[i-1] is indexed by a second attacker-controlled integer, so a huge X in XofY still panics

out_of_scope_notes: pkg/cookie/cookie.go:163-174 ClearCookie reflects every client-supplied cookie name beginning with the configured prefix back into a Set-Cookie header without validating it - a separate header-content issue, not pursued.
